title: Regional debenture borrowing and Wellesley tile drainage loan
subtitle: Special meeting also noted a debenture issue report, Persons Day, and a moment of reflection for peace in the Middle East.
overview: Regional Council held a short special meeting to finish the financing steps for a recent debenture issue. Council received a report on the successful $60 million ten-year debenture sale, which funds capital works for the Region and five of the seven area municipalities. Council then passed by-laws authorizing borrowing for Kitchener, Cambridge, Wellesley, Wilmot, Woolwich and the Region itself, along with a by-law combining them into one debenture series {{vote:m9}}.

Council also approved a loan under the Tile Drainage Act for the Township of Wellesley {{vote:m1}}. The Act lets agricultural landowners borrow for tile drainage projects at 6 percent interest. Staff said such loans had not come forward for some time because interest rates were lower, but the program becomes more attractive as rates rise.

For residents, the debenture approvals secure funding for local and regional capital projects. The Regional Chair also expressed sympathies over violence in the Middle East, marked Persons Day, and Council held a moment of reflection for peace. The meeting adjourned at 1:14 p.m.

decisions.detail: Council passed a by-law providing a loan under the Tile Drainage Act in line with Wellesley's rating by-law 31/2023, as set out in report COR-TRY-23-032.
Council enacted a by-law in respect of the Tile Drainage Debentures for the Township of Wellesley.
Council authorized one series of ten-year instalment debentures totalling $60,000,000, of which $18,023,000 may be raised through refinancing instalment debentures.
Council authorized ten-year instalment debentures of $26,265,000 for capital works of the Region.
Council authorized ten-year instalment debentures of $19,465,000 for Cambridge capital works, with $11,927,000 eligible for refinancing debentures.
Council authorized ten-year instalment debentures of $4,374,000 for Kitchener capital works.
Council authorized ten-year instalment debentures of $5,806,000 for Wilmot capital works, with $3,585,000 eligible for refinancing debentures.
Council authorized ten-year instalment debentures of $2,900,000 for a Wellesley capital work, with $1,786,000 eligible for refinancing debentures.

debate: There was little debate; the items were handled quickly and without delegations.
Staff said the debenture report reflected a successful recent sale in the debt capital markets that funds various capital works for the Region and five of the seven local municipalities.

On the tile drainage loan, staff said no such report had come forward in a long time because interest rates were lower in recent years. At the 6 percent rate set under the Act, the loans are now relatively attractive to landowners.
Staff noted the Act lets landowners borrow up to a set annual limit for tile drainage projects.
